paragraphs.source_en: When Ishida Mitsunari, accompanied by his newly acquired mistress, Osode, moved from Hakata Castle to Najima Castle in the nearby village of Tatara, the troops stationed in Korea had already received orders to withdraw and were fighting bitterly in various places even as they hurried toward their assembly points.

paragraphs.source_en: The first of the withdrawing ships entered Hakata Harbor on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month. Learning that the warships would arrive shortly after noon, Mitsunari left Najima Castle around the Hour of the Dragon and rode straight for the wharf. Temporary huts had been erected from Sode-no-hama to the Tatara shore to receive the returning army.

paragraphs.source_en: Osode felt that the return of these men would fill all Japan with a murderous air. Behind those ghastly faces, did human joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure remain as they had always been? Unable to bear the sight any longer, Osode closed her eyes, but dizziness suddenly swept over her and she staggered sideways. Fortunately, someone caught her.
